mac-proposal-VPN795.text: Proposal — VPN-795 · Mac menu-bar-only mode (no Dock icon)

mac-VPN795-panel-texts.text:
Panel footer: one new button, first in the row: "Open Securefield". It opens the main window and brings it to the front. Icon: SF Symbol macwindow, 15 pt, lightGray, like the other footer buttons. Shown in both modes (with and without the Dock icon).
Text: existing key menu.open — EN "Open Securefield", AR "فتح Securefield" (already in Localizable.xcstrings; not new). It is the button's tooltip and accessibility label.
Settings (gear) and Quit (power, "Quit Securefield") are already in this footer. No change to them.

mac-VPN795-board.text:
VPN-795 — how the user gets menu-bar-only mode
RECOMMENDED (b): a "Show in Dock" switch in Settings, default on. Nothing changes for current users. A user who wants a menu-bar-only app turns it off.
Other options:
(a) Always menu-bar-only, no setting. Not recommended: every user loses the Dock icon, Command-Tab and the app menu; a new user may not find the app after first launch.
(c) Dock icon only while a Securefield window is open. Not recommended: the icon comes and goes, which looks unstable; it also needs the new panel button.
(b) with default off is possible. Then first launch changes, and I add a first-launch hint frame (new text).

Every place that changes when "Show in Dock" is off:
• Main window at launch: it does not open when the Mac opens the app at login (Open at login). It opens when the user opens the app (Finder, Launchpad, Spotlight). If the code cannot tell a login launch from a user launch, it opens at every launch, as today.
• Open the main window again: new panel button "Open Securefield" (frames above). Opening the app again from Finder, Launchpad or Spotlight also opens it. There is no Dock icon to click.
• Settings: panel gear and main-window toolbar gear, as today. Command-comma works only while a Securefield window is in front.
• Quit: panel power button "Quit Securefield", as today. Closing the windows does not quit, as today.
• Help, Report, Premium, Connect: in the panel and the main window, as today. The app menu and the Connection menu are not visible, so their shortcuts have no visible menu.
• First launch: no change (default on). Welcome and VPN permission open as today.
• Command-Tab: Securefield is not in it. Each button that opens a window brings it to the front.
No change: main window, first launch, report, FAQ and document windows, the iPhone and iPad pages.

vpn907-iphone-block.text: Approved, not built — VPN-924 · VPN-907 · Connect opens the iOS prompt directly; help only after a decline

vpn907-iphone-row.text: Approved, not built — VPN-924 · VPN-907 · Connect, first press and decline (1 prompt, 2 help)

vpn907-iphone-flow.text:
iPhone flow (and iPad, same app):
1 First Connect: iOS shows its prompt at once. No screen of ours comes before it. This is how the app works today; it stays.
2 Don't Allow: the help sheet opens over Main. NEW. It replaces today's system alert "VPN configuration not added" (Try again / OK, MainScreen.VPNPermissionAlerts).
3 Try again: the sheet closes, then the app asks again, and iOS shows its prompt over Main (= frame 1). Allow → Connecting (current frame "Main · connecting"). Don't Allow again → the help sheet again.
4 ✕: the sheet closes. Back to Main, "Tap to connect" (current frame "Main · disconnected, free user"). The next Connect asks again. Nothing is remembered from a decline.
5 A management profile can block new VPN configurations; then iOS shows no prompt and the press ends as a decline. The last line of the help says where to look.
Not changed: the 20-second alert "Could not start the connection" (VPN-342).
Replaces: the system alert above. It has no frame on this canvas, so no current frame goes away on the iPhone and iPad pages.
The last line of the help after a decline (iPhone, iPad) is not built (board, 2026-11-18).

Texts — EN | AR. (app) = already in the app (Localizable.xcstrings), same EN and AR. (new) = new text. (system) = text of iOS or macOS, not ours.
Help after a decline, iPhone and iPad:
• VPN configuration not added | لم تتم إضافة إعداد VPN (app: VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_TITLE)
• Securefield can't connect without a VPN configuration. Tap Try again and choose Allow. | لا يمكن لـ Securefield الاتصال بدون إعداد VPN. اضغط «حاول مرة أخرى» واختر «سماح». (app: perm.deniedBody)
• The system window looks like this: | تظهر نافذة النظام هكذا: (new)
• 1 Tap Allow in the system window | اضغط «سماح» في نافذة النظام (app: perm.step1.ios)
• 2 Confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode | أكّد بـ Face ID أو Touch ID أو رمز الدخول (app: perm.step2.ios)
• 3 Securefield connects. Nothing else to set up | يتصل Securefield. لا يلزم أي إعداد آخر (app: perm.step3)
• If the iOS window doesn't appear, new VPN configurations may be blocked on this device; see Settings › General › VPN & Device Management. | إذا لم تظهر نافذة iOS، فقد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز؛ راجع الإعدادات › عام › VPN وإدارة الجهاز. (new: the second half of VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE as its own line)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: VPN_PERMISSION.TRY_AGAIN)
• ✕ = Close, as on the Report sheet (no visible text).
Help after a decline, Mac:
• VPN configuration not added | لم تتم إضافة إعداد VPN (app: perm.deniedTitle)
• Securefield can't connect without a VPN configuration. Click Try again and choose Allow. | لا يمكن لـ Securefield الاتصال بدون إعداد VPN. انقر «حاول مرة أخرى» واختر «سماح». (new: Mac wording; perm.deniedBody says "Tap")
• The system window looks like this: | تظهر نافذة النظام هكذا: (new, the same text as above)
• 1 Click Allow in the macOS window | انقر «سماح» في نافذة macOS (app: perm.step1.mac)
• 2 Confirm with Touch ID or your Mac password | أكّد بـ Touch ID أو كلمة مرور جهاز Mac (app: perm.step2.mac)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: perm.tryAgain)
• Open System Settings | فتح إعدادات النظام (app: perm.openSettings)
• Not now | ليس الآن (app text: CONNECTION_RATING.SKIP; new on the Mac)
System prompt (system; stand-in until the real screenshot, AR wording to confirm from it):
• “Securefield VPN” Would Like to Add VPN Configurations | يريد “Securefield VPN” إضافة إعدادات VPN
• All network activity on this iPhone (iPad, Mac) may be filtered or monitored when using VPN. | قد تتم تصفية كل نشاط الشبكة على هذا الـ iPhone (iPad، Mac) أو مراقبته عند استخدام VPN.
• Don’t Allow | عدم السماح   • Allow | سماح
No longer shown: perm.title, perm.body.mac, perm.step3 on the Mac, perm.continue (the Mac step before the prompt) and VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE (the iPhone and iPad alert). The keys can stay.

vpn907-iphone-picture.text:
The prompt picture. The board asked for the real iOS prompt picture. No screenshot of it is on the runner, and the runner may not open Apple pages. So every prompt in these frames (over the screens and inside the help) is a STAND-IN drawing in the dark look. Before the build, SecurefieldiOS takes the real prompt on SecureField's own test devices (iPhone, iPad and Mac), EN and AR, and the help uses a crop of it as an image asset (Assets › Images, one per platform and language). I then swap the drawing for the crop on this canvas. The green ring around Allow is ours (lightGreen #35DF91, 2.5 px, radius 12), drawn over the crop.

Tokens and components: GradientBackground; the Report sheet (iPhone radius 40/40/60/60, iPad form sheet radius 12); GradientBorderCard (iceBlue, radius 18, border gradient); the PermissionView step circles (darkBlue #0073C5, 26 pt, white bold); text lightGray #D1DCEA and white; RadialGradientButton green; Mac: PrimaryButtonStyle (#33A9FE → #1EB972), links lightGreen. No new token. New component: PromptPicture (card + crop of the system prompt + ring on Allow).
Contrast: white on darkBlue 4.93:1; lightGray on the card 7.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact because they are the app's own buttons: white on the green button 2.37:1, white on the Mac button 2.55:1 (see Proposals on VPN-907).

vpn923-mac-contrast.text:
VPN-923 — Mac primary button: contrast per state (WCAG 2.x; text Red Hat Display Bold 15 pt = normal text, needs 4.5:1).
Measured from the values, at every point of the gradient; for pressed and disabled the button is laid over the window background (graphite #172231 → black), and the worst point counts.

TODAY (white text, #FFFFFF):
• normal: 2.55:1 (lightBlue end 2.55, green end 2.55, middle 2.59) — FAIL
• pressed (opacity 0.85): 2.40:1 worst point — FAIL
• disabled (opacity 0.4): 1.75:1 worst point — FAIL (WCAG does not require contrast for a disabled control; the board asked for 4.5:1 in every state)

PROPOSAL (drawn in these frames):
• normal: text graphite #172231 on lightBlue #33A9FE → green #1EB972: 6.15:1 worst point (6.30 at the blue end, 6.29 at the green end) — PASS
• pressed: as today, opacity 0.85 and scale 0.98: 4.79:1 worst point — PASS
• disabled: fill surfaceHigh (white 10 %, no gradient), text lightGray #D1DCEA: 8.54:1 over graphite, 12.61:1 over black — PASS
Pixel check on the renders of these 16 frames (Chromium; solid text colour against the fill at each column under the label; worst column): normal 6.10–6.16:1; pressed 4.74–4.81:1 (Welcome lowest: the map shows through); disabled 11.07:1. Today's frames, same check: 2.58:1.

Why dark text and not a darker gradient:
• Dark text keeps the brand gradient exactly, and it uses an existing token (graphite). The app already has a dark-text button: PremiumButtonStyle (#1B1305 on the yellow gradient).
• A darker gradient needs two new colours. darkBlue #0073C5 → darkGreen #198F57 gives only 4.11:1 at the green end. #0073C5 → #167F4E passes at rest (4.93) but fails when pressed (4.38).
Tokens: lightBlue, green, graphite, surfaceHigh, lightGray. No new token.

Build (SecurefieldiOS, Mac only):
• PrimaryButtonStyle (native/Design/Brand.swift): .foregroundStyle(Brand.graphite) when enabled. Disabled: Capsule fill Brand.surfaceHigh and text Brand.lightGray, in place of .opacity(0.4). Pressed: no change.
• ConnectStyle (native/MacApp/MacPanel.swift), Connect side (on == false): text Brand.graphite. The Disconnect side (white 10 % fill, white text) does not change.
• A ProgressView in the button (Report, while sending) takes the same disabled fill.
• iPhone and iPad: no change.

vpn907np-iphone-flow.text:

2 iOS shows no prompt (for example a management profile blocks new VPN configurations, or iOS cannot load or save the configuration). Refused while the app was inactive (the prompt was up) = decline → the round-1 help sheet.

4 ✕: the sheet closes. Back to Main, "Tap to connect". The next Connect asks again.
In the iOS Simulator every Connect ends here (the Simulator never shows the VPN prompt). Design review and QA see this screen first.
Scrolling (approval item 41, build rule in VPN-924): the content scrolls only when it does not fit; Try again stays fixed. These frames show the case that fits.
Replaces: no current frame. Today this case ends in the system alert "VPN configuration not added", which has no frame on this canvas.

vpn1058-iphone-block.text: Proposal — VPN-1058 · premium icon in place of the "PREMIUM" tag in the free user's server list

vpn1058-iphone-row.text: Proposal — VPN-1058 · Server list · free user (today, then proposal; EN, then AR)

vpn1058-iphone-icon.text:
Proposal — VPN-1058: the premium icon in place of the "PREMIUM" tag (board, 11-21).
Where: each premium row in the free user's server list (ServerItem, ServerListScreen.swift). Today the PremiumMark pill (SERVER_LIST.PREMIUM_MARK, "PREMIUM" / "مميز") sits before the signal bars. The proposal puts the icon in the same place. Flag, name, signal bars, radio button and spacing (12 pt while the mark shows) stay as today.
Icon: Design System icons/Premium (assets/Icons/Premium.svg, the app asset icons/Premium). It is the crown at the top left of the iPhone Main screen, the free user's way to Premium. So the user already knows it as "premium".
Size: 20 × 20 pt, scaledToFit. That is the height of today's pill (Caption line, 2 pt padding top and bottom), so the row height (63 pt on a 390 pt phone) and the alignment do not change. The signal bars are 25.2 pt and the radio 29.4 pt, so the crown stays the smallest mark in the row.
Colour: the asset's own stroke, lightYellow #FAC762 (text.quaternary / border.secondary, the premium colour; the orange radio ring of the same row has it). No tint. Contrast on the page background (#172231 to #000000): 10.2:1 to 13.4:1, above 3:1 for icons.
Arabic: the crown is symmetric and is not mirrored. In RTL it stays before the signal bars in reading order (left of them on screen).
Who sees it: only a free user, only on a premium server (Server.showsPremiumMark). A premium user sees no tag today and no icon in the proposal. Tap on the row opens the Premium screen, as today.
Not changed: the two-column iPad list (WideServerList, heading "Premium" with a crown), the Mac app, the onboarding.

vpn1058-iphone-voiceover.text:
VoiceOver (step 3).
Today: the row is one button. VoiceOver reads the name and the tag text: "Netherlands, PREMIUM, button" / "هولندا، مميز، زر".
Proposal: the icon gets an accessibility label with the same catalog text, SERVER_LIST.PREMIUM_MARK ("PREMIUM" / "مميز"). So VoiceOver reads the same words as today. No new text, no new translation.
Without a label, VoiceOver would read the asset name ("icons/Premium") or nothing. So the label is required.
Keep the accessibilityIdentifier "server_list.premium_mark" on the icon, so UI tests find it as today.

vpn1058-iphone-mark.text: Proposal — VPN-1058 (below): the premium icon (icons/Premium, 20 pt) in place of the "PREMIUM" tag on locked rows. These free-user frames stay until the board approves.
